correctness.rationale: Derived exact update equations from every vertex neighborhood. Odd total size produces a uniform clique immediately; even total size has complement only on the central population. The independent module is uniform except at clique half-tie. Complete case analysis yields T<=3 and exactly the stated strictly asymmetric central layer for T=3; Vandermonde counts it. Direct recurrent-state classification yields two fixed points and the full explicit primitive two-cycle census. The central binomial approximation follows from Stirling and negligible endpoint/tie ratios. Replayed 1,835,012 direct labeled trajectories in 120 graph-size cases and 313,600 population signatures in 1024 graph-size cases from the standalone verification script, all passed. Finite tests are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The strict-neighbor-majority voting time on an infinite natural graph family is given a sharp all-parameter bound and a new parity/imbalance transition (Tmax jumps to 3 only for a>b, even order and b>=3). A closed exact binomial expression counts every maximal-delay labeled state and yields an inverse-square-root rare-event asymptotic, contrasting worst-case and typical convergence times. The phenomenon does not occur in the earlier balanced family, and the formula is motivated by the threshold central layer rather than an arbitrary slice.
